raw.markdown:
# Sclerotherapy — Authorization Guide

## CPT Codes — Sclerotherapy

| CPT | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 36468 | Single or multiple injections of sclerosing solutions, spider veins (telangiectasia); limb or trunk |
| 36470 | Injection of sclerosing solution; single vein |
| 36471 | Injection of sclerosing solution; multiple veins, same leg |
| 36465 | Injection of non-compounded foam sclerosant with ultrasound compression maneuvers to guide dispersion of the injectate, inclusive of all imaging guidance and monitoring; single incompetent extremity truncal vein (e.g., great saphenous vein, accessory saphenous vein) |
| 36466 | Injection of non-compounded foam sclerosant; multiple incompetent truncal veins, same leg, each additional |
| 93971 | Duplex scan of extremity veins, unilateral (pre-procedure) |

Note: CPT 36468 is typically not covered by most insurance plans (considered cosmetic for telangiectasias). Coverage is more likely for 36470/36471 (varicose veins) and 36465/36466 (foam for truncal veins).

## ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes

| ICD-10 | Description |
| --- | --- |
| I83.811 | Varicose veins of right lower extremity with pain |
| I83.812 | Varicose veins of left lower extremity with pain |
| I83.10 | Varicose veins with inflammation, unspecified lower extremity |
| I83.001 | Varicose veins of right lower extremity with ulcer of thigh |
| I87.2 | Venous insufficiency (chronic) (peripheral) |
| I78.1 | Nevus, non-neoplastic (spider angioma — for telangiectasias) |
| I83.90 | Asymptomatic varicose veins of unspecified lower extremity |

## Coverage Considerations by Vessel Type

### Telangiectasias / Spider Veins (C1) — Generally NOT Covered

- Most payers consider sclerotherapy of telangiectasias cosmetic (CEAP C1)
- Medicare does not cover CPT 36468 for spider veins
- Some payers may cover if associated with symptomatic venous insufficiency (C2+)
- Document any associated symptoms (bleeding, thrombophlebitis) to support medical necessity

### Varicose Veins (C2+) — Covered with Medical Necessity

- CEAP C2 or higher with symptomatic venous insufficiency
- Duplex ultrasound confirming reflux (required by most payers)
- Compression stocking trial ≥3–6 weeks with documented failure
- Foam sclerotherapy (CPT 36465/36466) requires ultrasound guidance documentation

### Medicare (CMS)

- CPT 36468 (spider veins): Not covered — cosmetic
- CPT 36470/36471: Covered for symptomatic varicose veins with medical necessity
- CPT 36465/36466: Covered for truncal vein foam sclerotherapy with duplex guidance
- Requires documentation of symptoms, duplex findings, and failed conservative therapy

### Documentation Checklist

- CEAP classification documented in office note
- Duplex ultrasound report (for varicose veins and foam sclerotherapy)
- Compression stocking prescription and compliance record
- Symptom documentation (pain, swelling, skin changes)
- Photographs of varicosities
